newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German May jobless data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German May jobless data.

text.p: The German labour office said on Friday that pan-German unadjusted jobless grew by an adjusted 56,000 in May, for an unadjusted jobless rate of 11.1 percent. The total adjusted figure was 4.256 million.
Following are analysts' comments on the data.

KAREN KRICKS-BRUNNLIEB, HEAD OF FIXED INCOME, TRINKAUS CAPITAL MANAGEMENT: "This is a poor number and the average unemployment figure for this year may now come out at more than 4.3 million we had forecast so far. We would now expect it to come out at 4.35 million. I would expect an improvement at the earliest in the autumn."
ULRICH BECKMANN, SENIOR ECONOMIST, DEUTSCHE BANK RESEARCH:

"These figures are disappointing compared with our forecast, we have to accept that. We were hoping for a stabilisation of the labour market and I must say that an increase of 56,000 does not fit into our growth scenario for the economy. What we are seeing is that the construction sector weighs very heavily on the labour market. In any case, this is bad news for Mr Waigel."
ADRIAN OWENS, EUROPEAN ECONOMIST, JULIUS BAER INVESTMENTS:

"The last three months had signalled that perhaps unemployment was levelling out, so this is a setback. However, I think that in a broader context we are seeing a stabilisation and will see that increasingly in the latter part of the year."
